B.finding: Official solution fixes one binary state per row/column, toggles across A cells, checks toroidal parity, and imposes B-cell consistency as a bipartite graph; consistent answer is 2^(number of connected components). This independently matches the frozen parity-DSU mechanism.

C.finding: Official solution characterizes a cut exactly as absence of a backward W->B edge across the prefix, matching the frozen p-state invariant. It then uses inclusion-exclusion plus divide-and-conquer FFT for O(N log^2 N), confirming the frozen O(N^2) implementation is not constraint-safe.

D.finding: Official solution uses the same town-potential formulation, then derives laminar interval conditions and a two-pointer/BIT/Zobrist query algorithm in O((N+M) log N + Q). This corroborates correctness of the frozen feasibility semantics while confirming its per-query rebuild is non-scalable.
